scope: Aardman, Bluey and Pixar; nine source sheets and registered contact sheets where present
method: Visual comparison of actual-alpha dark diagnostic composites, 12-frame contact sheets, and original acting-study source art. No artwork or runtime modified.
limitations: Still images cannot establish temporal smoothness, browser frame pacing or voice sync.
Source pixel uniqueness and exact layer reconstruction belong to the compiler checks.

examples.observations: ImageGen transparency cleanup resolves previous real alpha haze. Round eye identity, upper-lid silhouette closure, full closed arcs at frame 3 and raised eyebrow at frames 6-8 are coherent. Closed mouth supports listening. Registered contact has stable mouth placement, no visible crop cuts, and compatible first/last pose scale.

Half-lids close to a true pupil-free lid drawing at frame 3; neutral mouth supports dry disbelief. Asymmetry at frames 6-7 is intentional. Registered first/last poses have compatible scale and placement.

Closed eyes at frame 3 are valid. Upward gaze returns at frame 11 and closed mouth matches start. Frames 2 and 3 are visually close; the acting beat is mostly a small smile, suitable for quiet rather than emphatic realisation.

Concerned eye silhouette is retained during the blink. Full close at frame 3, reopening at 4-5, then modest smile at 6-8. End mouth returns to closed neutral, with no happiness imposed on concerned rest.

Full close is a cheerful upward lid arc at frame 3. Surprise opens into a smile at 6-8; this is visually distinct from reassurance. It reads clearly in stills, but the surprise-to-smile accent has only two adjacent drawings and should be judged at playback speed.

Drooping half-lids, asymmetric questioning gaze and slanted closed mouth preserve tentative emotion. No smile is introduced. Fully closed arc at frame 3; first/last neutral-half-lid poses are compatible.

Upward gaze and small return smile match the reference. Full close at frame 3 is a pupil-free arc, not a shrunken pupil. Half-blinks retain a heavy upper-lid cap at 1,2,4; acceptable stylization, but less delicate than the Bluey examples.

Closed blink and flat mouth preserve concentration. Clear sideways checking silhouette at frame 7. The return from side-gaze 7 to forward 8 is a relatively large pose change; inspect at actual speed before calling the motion smooth.

Asymmetric starting eyes and smiling upward gaze reproduce the original discovery idea. Full close at 3; mouth separates cleanly. Smile is brief at frame 7 before neutral return at 8, so hold length may need adjustment after motion review.

summary: Nine independent source/contact reviews completed. No blocking visual defects remain. Five minor stylistic or timing caveats are recorded for motion review.
